H-OS-L1.name: Pebble
H-OS-L1.sphere: Pebble (H-OS-L1) has the largest sample (n=95), mean 7.15 ± 1.78 (strong confidence) with a right‑skewed distribution; 48 responses are 8‑10. Qualitative feedback (29 respondents) notes settle times around 10 min and strong rhythm comfort. YouTube views are 30, the highest in the library, though retention data are missing. AutoGluon predicts 6.859, about 0.3 points below the observed mean, suggesting real‑world efficacy exceeds model expectations.
H-OS-L1.sphere_plain: Pebble is highly effective for overstimulation, though only a few people have found it so far.

H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall
H-OS-L2.sphere: Rainfall (H-OS-L2) recorded n=51, mean 6.92 ± 1.73 (strong confidence) with a narrow peak at score 7. Qualitative data (21 respondents) show consistent 10‑min settle times and primarily liked music. YouTube views are 5. AutoGluon’s overstim prediction (6.859) is slightly below the observed mean.
H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Rainfall offers consistent relief for overstimulation and is a bit more modest in its impact.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier
H-OS-L3.sphere: Glacier (H-OS-L3) gathered n=47, mean 7.04 ± 1.68 (meaningful confidence) with a right‑tail of high scores (3 10s, 6 9s). Qualitative respondents often used it while trying to sleep, indicating cross‑zone use. Rhythm opinions split evenly between balanced and very settling. YouTube views are 8. AutoGluon predicts 6.859, under‑scoring the observed performance.
H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Glacier often helps especially when people try to sleep, delivering strong relief for many.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow
H-AX-L1.sphere: Meadow (H-AX-L1) collected n=67 responses with a mean of 7.22 ± 1.93 (strong confidence). The distribution is mildly bimodal, clustering around scores 8‑9 and 5‑7, reflecting mixed entry states. Qualitative input (23 respondents) notes typical settle times of ~10 min and strong rhythm appreciation. YouTube reach is minimal (7 views, no retention data). AutoGluon predicts 7.838 for the anxiety zone, about 0.6 points above the observed mean, suggesting the model expects higher efficacy as listener mix stabilises.
H-AX-L1.sphere_plain: Listeners report Meadow quickly eases anxiety, with most feeling better after about ten minutes.

H-AX-L2.name: Cottage
H-AX-L2.sphere: Cottage (H-AX-L2) achieved n=48, mean 6.94 ± 1.62 (meaningful confidence) with a tight peak at score 7. Faster settle times (~5 min) were reported by 9 of 20 respondents. Music opinions were more polarized than L1, while rhythm remained balanced. No YouTube data are available. AutoGluon’s anxiety‑zone prediction (7.838) exceeds the observed mean, indicating a modest performance gap.
H-AX-L2.sphere_plain: Cottage also helps anxiety, though the effect shows up a bit more slowly for some people.

H-AX-L3.name: Valley
H-AX-L3.sphere: Valley (H-AX-L3) gathered n=36, mean 7.08 ± 1.89 (meaningful confidence) and exhibits a bimodal shape similar to L1, with a right‑tail of high scores. Qualitative reports (20 respondents) show the longest settle times (~10 min) among the sub‑series, consistent with its extended DESCENT arc. YouTube views are 4, underscoring limited discovery. AutoGluon predicts 7.838, modestly above the observed mean.
H-AX-L3.sphere_plain: Valley gives a solid anxiety relief, especially for those who stay with it longer.

H-CR-L1.name: Anchor
H-CR-L1.sphere: Anchor (H-CR-L1) recorded n=43, mean 6.35 ± 1.70 (meaningful confidence), the lowest mean in HEALING. Scores cluster broadly from 4‑8, with a modest peak at 8. Qualitative data (24 respondents) show 8 significant‑improvement reports, chiefly from caregivers, and rapid settle times (5‑10 min). YouTube views are 6. AutoGluon forecasts a crisis‑zone score of 7.955, over 1.5 points higher than observed, highlighting a potential caregiver‑report bias.
H-CR-L1.sphere_plain: Anchor seems to give noticeable relief in crisis moments, especially as reported by caregivers.

H-CR-L2.name: Harbor

AutoGluon predicts 7.955, again above observed, suggesting the crisis model may overestimate efficacy for this cohort.
H-CR-L2.sphere_plain: Harbor provides steady, moderate improvement for acute distress, with mixed music feedback.

H-CR-L3.name: Horizon
H-CR-L3.sphere: Horizon (H-CR-L3) obtained n=27, mean 6.52 ± 1.91 (meaningful confidence). The distribution includes a small high‑score tail (two 10s) and rapid settlement (7 of 19 within 1 min). H-CR-L3.sphere_plain: Horizon works fast for many, though a few listeners didn’t like the music.

H-SL-L1.name: Lantern

AutoGluon predicts 7.539, modestly below observed.
H-SL-L1.sphere_plain: Lantern quickly helps people relax for sleep, with many rating it as very calming.

sphere_commentary.overview:
Outcome data across 1000 listeners suggest distinct efficacy patterns among the three series, with HEALING showing the most consistently strong responses.
• HEALING protocols average 6.98 mean score and exhibit the lowest coefficient of variation, indicating reliable entrainment.
• THRIVING protocols reach a comparable mean (6.96) but display broader spread, with several high‑peak HOLD designs.
• TRANSFORMING protocols lag slightly (6.59 mean) and show the greatest variance, matching expectations for ASCENT arcs.
• Low‑view, high‑score protocols (e.g., H-OS-L1) hint at undiscovered efficacy, while high‑variance low‑n protocols flag population‑mismatch signals.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
The three series display efficacy trends that mirror their therapeutic intent.
• HEALING DESCENT protocols deliver the most consistent improvements across anxiety, overstimulation, crisis, and sleep zones.
• THRIVING HOLD protocols generate the highest peak scores (e.g., T-FC-L3) but also the widest score dispersion, suggesting sensitivity to listener state and groove preference.
• TRANSFORMING ASCENT protocols exhibit the greatest spread, with some (X-MD-L3) achieving high means despite high variance, and others (X-MC-L3) showing low means and bimodality.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols stand out as statistical or qualitative outliers warranting closer scrutiny.
• X-MD-L3 shows extreme drift (sim=0.507) and the highest observed std (2.38) for n=13, indicating possible sample instability.
• H-CR-L1 records a low mean (6.35) yet the highest proportion of qualitative “significant improvement” reports, suggesting caregiver‑report bias.
• H-OS-L1 combines a high mean (7.15) with very few YouTube views (30), flagging an undiscovered high‑efficacy protocol.
• T-FC-L3 displays a right‑tail cluster at score 10 alongside a lower‑mid cluster, hinting at bimodal response.
• H-SL-L2 rhythm opinions are split “too busy,” aligning with its higher std and indicating groove friction.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Targeted protocol refinements emerge from convergent signals across analyses.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MD-L3 (n=13) – high variance and drift; action: conduct subgroup analysis and test an L2 variant with a gentler ascent slope.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-OS-L1 (n=95) – strong outcomes, low discovery; action: boost YouTube promotion and experiment with thumbnail optimization.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-MB-L2 (n=22) – rhythm‑busy split and high std; action: record a VOL002 variant with simplified percussion.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-CR-L1 (n=43) – qualitative–quantitative tension; action: separate caregiver‑reported outcomes from direct listener surveys via routing logic.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 (n=10) – low mean, high variance, drift; action: redesign groove or length, and test a hybrid L2 version aligned to mood‑elevation zone.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Embedding drift and clustering reveal analytic stability and similarity patterns across the library.
• CROSS‑RUN DRIFT: All 30 protocols show notable drift (<0.85 similarity); X-MD-L3 (0.507) and H-SL-L1 (0.530) are the most unstable.
• CROSS‑PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: Tight pairs include T-FC-L1↔T-FC-L2 (0.878) and H-SL-L1↔H-SL-L2 (0.869); H-OS-L3, T-FC-L3, and T-CF-L3 are analytically distinct.
• Confidence note: Drift estimates are based on only two runs; a third run would improve reliability.

by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Anchor seems to give noticeable relief in crisis moments, especially as reported by caregivers.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Harbor provides steady, moderate improvement for acute distress, with mixed music feedback.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Horizon works fast for many, though a few listeners didn’t like the music.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: Pebble is highly effective for overstimulation, though only a few people have found it so far.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Rainfall offers consistent relief for overstimulation and is a bit more modest in its impact.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Glacier often helps especially when people try to sleep, delivering strong relief for many.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Lantern quickly helps people relax for sleep, with many rating it as very calming.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Hammock is steady for sleep but some find its rhythm a little busy.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Midnight settles sleep fairly fast, though a few listeners notice a busy rhythm.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Ember supports creative flow with a calm, steady effect.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Current feels a bit sharper for creativity, and listeners love the music.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Aurora boosts creative flow the most, with many noticing strong improvement.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Compass helps focus but some listeners feel the rhythm is a bit distracting.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Waypoint improves focus with balanced rhythm and mixed music feelings.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: Summit gives the strongest focus boost, though it takes longer to settle.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Stone supports balance nicely, though settling can take a while.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Axis tries to aid balance but its rhythm feels busy to many users.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Orbit offers moderate balance help with mixed rhythm feedback.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Cavern can improve mental clarity for some, but a few felt worse.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Starlight generally settles the mind well and feels very calming.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Cosmos shows mixed results; some listeners improve, others don’t like it.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Footpath aims to boost motivation but results are modest and varied.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Trail offers a gentle motivation lift, though the effect is modest.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Switchback can raise motivation strongly for some, but responses are split.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Breeze lifts mood and energy, and many listeners love the music.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Sunrise also boosts mood, with a few noting a slightly busy rhythm.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Updraft gives a mild mood lift, but several users felt no change.
